name: Theodore Roosevelt
description: US president associated with the Square Deal, antitrust enforcement, conservation and an expanded international role.

axes.brief: Competitive elections and public accountability accompanied an expansive presidency.
axes.counter: Executive discretion and unequal voting access qualified modern universal-democratic analogies.

axes.brief: Regulatory enforcement and order coexisted with civil institutions and public criticism.
axes.counter: The Brownsville dismissals and paternalist regulation qualify liberal tolerance.

axes.brief: Americanisation and common language were priorities.
axes.counter: Recognition of selected minority leaders did not imply general cultural accommodation.

axes.brief: Economic immigration continued with national screening and Asian restrictions.
axes.counter: Managed immigration is separate from demanding cultural assimilation.

axes.brief: Naval power, intervention and deterrence were central tools.
axes.counter: Mediation of the Russo-Japanese War and diplomacy also mattered.

axes.brief: US sovereignty and regional influence prevailed over supranational authority.
axes.counter: International mediation and commercial cooperation were accepted.

axes.brief: Private enterprise was retained while utilities and public lands received special treatment.
axes.counter: Trust regulation did not by itself make business publicly owned.

axes.brief: Protective trade institutions and national development coexisted with foreign commerce.
axes.counter: Not every domestic business was entitled to indefinite protection.

axes.brief: Competition coexisted with antitrust, food regulation and strategic public coordination.
axes.counter: The Square Deal was not ordinary compulsory production quotas.

axes.brief: Worker protection and criticism of excessive corporate privilege qualified laissez-faire distribution.
axes.counter: Many stronger progressive tax proposals belong to his later post-presidential platform and are excluded.

axes.brief: Civil government and personal religion coexisted with public moral appeals.
axes.counter: There was no clerical legal veto or a national religious constitution.

axes.brief: Conventional family roles and motherhood were praised.
axes.counter: Women’s public participation and some reform did not eliminate conventional sex roles.

axes.brief: Federal habitat and forest conservation constrained development.
axes.counter: The Panama Canal and productive resource management show substantial support for infrastructure.

axes.brief: Federal corporate regulation and public lands strengthened national authority.
axes.counter: State constitutions and ordinary local policing remained.

axes.brief: Racial hierarchy and inherited fitness arguments coexisted with training and moral improvement.
axes.counter: Later eugenic correspondence is excluded; precise IQ, attention and stress claims remain uncertain historical analogies.
